title: Word counts in a StringMap
show: (fun m -> String.concat " " (List.map (fun (w, n) -> w ^ ":" ^ string_of_int n) (StringMap.bindings m)))
hints: The starter throws away every map that `StringMap.add` returns, so `m` stays empty. A map never changes, so you have to keep the new one.
Use `List.fold_left`: the accumulator is the map so far, starting at `StringMap.empty`.
`List.fold_left (fun m w -> let n = match StringMap.find_opt w m with Some n -> n | None -> 0 in StringMap.add w (n + 1) m) StringMap.empty words`.
explain: The reference folds over the words with the map as the accumulator. Each step looks up the old count with `find_opt` and returns `StringMap.add w (n + 1) m`, a new map, which the fold hands to the next step. `StringMap.bindings` lists the keys in sorted order, so no sort is needed.
